![](bbox=[0.13, 0.05, 0.56, 0.33])

**Figure 7.6** Multilayer Boltzmann machine for handwritten digit recognition and generation. The image has 28 × 28 = 784 pixels, which can be white or black. The goal is to classify the digit based on the ten output units (0–9). From G. E. Hinton, “Learning Multiple Layers of Representation,” *Trends in Cognitive Sciences* 11 (2007): 428–434, figure 1.

![](bbox=[0.13, 0.475, 0.7, 0.765])

**Figure 7.7** Input layer patterns generated by a multilayer Boltzmann machine trained to recognize handwritten digits. Each line was generated by clamping one of the ten output units (figure 7.6), and the input layer continuously morphed between the examples shown above. None of these digits were in the training set—they were “hallucinated” by the Teh of the trained network. From G. E. Hinton, S. Osindero, and Y. Teh, “A Fast Learning Algorithm for Deep Belief Nets,” *Neural Computation* 18 (2006): 1527–1554 figure 8.
